newsitem.title: UK: Waste Management signs option to sell plant.
newsitem.headline: Waste Management signs option to sell plant.

text.p: Waste Management International Plc said on Wednesday its German subsidiary had granted German energy group VEW AG and one of its subsidiaries an option to buy its waste-to-energy plant at Hamm in Germany for 88 million stg.

The group said in a statement that it had the right to require VEW to purchase the facility for 76 million stg and both options were exercisable on or before January 2, 1998 but could be extended for a further three months "under certain circumstances".

WWI said the deal was structured as an option to enable VEW to work with the city of Hamm, the main supplier of waste to the plant, to modify the terms of the current supply agreement which runs through 2004.

"If the option is exercised, payment will be made in cash, and the proceeds will be used by WWI to reduce debt," the group said, adding that any sale "would most likely be completed in the first quarter of 1998".
It said it would not make a significant gain or loss on the transaction.

"We have taken the decision to sell the Hamm facility for strategic reasons. WWI will continue to have significant operations in Germany and we remain firmly committed to our business in this country," WWI's chief executive Bo Gabrielson said.

WWI provides solid and hazardous waste management services, including collection, transportation, storage, treatment, recycling, incineration and waste-to-energy services. It operates in 10 European countries.
